timeline.title: 7-video external evaluation
timeline.summary: Frozen baseline FAILING 96-99% on all clips incl 2 confirmed normal prints; 2 spaghetti detected.

timeline.title: normal augmentation (Exp3)
timeline.summary: +333 normal/7 sources -> held-out FPR 1.000->0.258; misses confirmed spaghetti; SKZ failure recall 0.10.

runtime: C++ behaviorally equivalent to Python POC (states/events exact; raw-P within 0.15 decoder floor)
inference pipeline works end to end
performance sufficient at 1 fps cadence on dev machine (infer ~2.2 ms; 19-53 fps)
model: failure detection transfers to independent footage (SKZ recall 0.966; spaghetti clips)
severe out-of-domain normal false-positive behavior (FPR 1.000; 96-99% on confirmed normals)
target-domain normal augmentation substantially reduces it (1.000->0.258; 7-8x on clips)
adding a small failure tail reverses it (back to 1.000; 39-54% on clips)
simple count-based balancing does not produce a stable operating point
data: original public dataset insufficiently representative of target-domain normal footage
continuous fixed-camera footage substantially more informative than arbitrary stills (supported)
source diversity matters more than frame count (supported)
two-camera failure augmentation insufficient and caused style/domain overfitting (supported)
target-domain normal data is the dominant missing ingredient (supported)

not_proven: no demonstrated under-extrusion robustness on truly independent target-domain footage

architecture_assessment.conclusion: Keep the architecture; the training data is the primary unresolved problem. No evidence justifies replacement.
